clue.text: Lead putting pressure on bad back

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure
lumbago is a painful lower back condition; 'on' places pressure first in this down clue

explanation.surface: Someone with a sore back is being hurried or burdened by a person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as someone in charge or a leash, but it is the metal-coloured mineral. In a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an old name for graphite, the black mineral once mistaken for the metal and used in pencil 'leads'.

clue.text: Runs out of passage in bar

indicators.note: a thing that runs out of somewhere has left it, so that letter goes missing from the word

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an excerpt is a passage taken from a longer text

explanation.surface: Someone runs out of a corridor into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a noun for a pub but is the preposition meaning 'apart from'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition 'bar' means apart from or excluding, exactly the sense of the word in 'all except one'.

clue.text: Means to go after key way to dodge reality

indicators.note: going after means following behind, so this piece is placed second in the answer

blocks.note: Escape is a key on a computer keyboard
a mechanism is a means or method of doing something

explanation.surface: Instructions for finding a way out once a key has been located.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts with the second piece: 'Means' is told to follow the key, so the keyboard key comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological habit or outlet used to avoid facing unpleasant facts is called by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Syringes found in soft sloppy nappies

indicators.note: sloppy means messy and careless, so the letters land in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
taken as written

explanation.surface: Medical needles turn up inside a baby's soggy nappies, a nappy being a British diaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Syringes' suggests hypodermics, but a syrinx is also the Greek name for the reed pipes of the god Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A syrinx is the classical name for a set of graded reed pipes played by blowing across them, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Move in or out — I can take anything

indicators.note: out here means out of place or disordered, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An easygoing person says they'll cope with anything, whether moving in or out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person, as the creature itself might describe its diet.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plants and meat, so it could boast that it will happily eat any food at all.

clue.text: Sovereigns containing flaw uncovered in slacks

indicators.note: stripped of its covering, a word loses its outside letters and keeps its core
one thing containing another holds it inside, so the kings wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R; here the plural word itself
the inner letters of flaw

explanation.surface: Kings with a stain on their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slacks' looks like trousers but is the verb meaning eases off.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken or loosen is to ease tension, so 'slacks' as a verb matches loosening or unwinding.

clue.text: Counterfeiters partly raised bond yet again

indicators.note: only part of the word is used, so the letters lie inside it
in a down clue, raising letters lifts them upward so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Forgers have raised part of a government bond issue once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests a financial certificate, but here it is the verb to tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To bond is to tie together, and doing so once more is to tie up again.

clue.text: Cool political movement accepted by a doctor

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the group sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the Palestine Liberation Organization
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A calm political campaign is welcomed by a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Cool' as a noun means composure under pressure, the self-assurance this word names.

clue.text: City guides delivered through headphones

indicators.note: what comes through headphones is heard, not read, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to guide is to lead

explanation.surface: A city tour with guides piped into visitors' earphones.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major English city in West Yorkshire, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Snooker fashion line replaced by Miyake's leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the letters at the front of the name
one thing replaced by another is swapped out, so letters are exchanged

blocks.note: style is fashion
L is the abbreviation for line
the leading pair of letters of the designer's name

explanation.surface: A snooker player's fashion line is overtaken by designs from Issey Miyake's top people.
explanation.walkthrough: Issey Miyake was a Japanese fashion designer, which fits the surface. 'Snooker' is a verb here: to block or thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a player is blocked from a direct shot; figuratively both verbs mean thwart or obstruct someone.

clue.text: Dessert that may appear before diner's order?

definitions.text: Dessert that may appear before diner's order?

blocks.clueFragment: Dessert that may appear before diner's order?
blocks.note: surface reading: a pudding served before the main meal is ordered
setter's reading: the pudding's name comes before 'order' in the phrase meaning perfectly tidy

explanation.walkthrough: Something in 'apple-pie order' is neat and perfectly arranged; the dessert's name is the word that precedes 'order'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a classic baked pudding of fruit in pastry, and its name forms the idiom for immaculate neatness.

clue.text: Wit in extremely rare company broadcast

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word
something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: first and last letters of rare
a party is a company of people

explanation.surface: A clever remark made on a radio show featuring a very unusual guest list.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversation and banter, so it is a form of verbal wit.

clue.text: A good deal one rejected following P45, say

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so these letters run in the opposite direction
coming after places this group behind the letter it follows

blocks.note: taken as written
lots means a good deal
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A redundancy package is turned down after being handed a P45, the British form given to someone leaving a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'P45' looks like one unit, but P is taken as written and '45, say' is the definition: a Colt .45 is a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: A .45 is a handgun of that calibre, so it is an example of this kind of firearm.

clue.text: Zoom lens seeks out area with no fogging?

indicators.note: out here means disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A photographer's zoom lens seeks out an area where the view isn't misted up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that fogging means smog from coal fires rather than a misted lens.
explanation.definitionFit: Such zones were set up in British cities where burning coal or wood that produces smoke and smog is banned.

clue.text: More genuine after moneylender loses 50%

indicators.note: losing half of something means only the other half of its letters remains

blocks.note: since means after, as in 'since then'
a usurer lends money at high interest

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more honest once a loan shark takes a big loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and honest, so the comparative form means more genuine.

clue.text: Used device beset by endless repair

indicators.note: without its ends, a word keeps only its inner letters
something beset is surrounded on all sides, so it sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: repair as a verb is remedy, whose inner letters are kept
a ploy is a cunning device or stratagem

explanation.surface: A worn gadget surrounded by a never-ending repair job.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection works on a synonym, not the printed word: repair becomes remedy before its ends go.
explanation.definitionFit: Employed means put to use or made use of, matching the past participle 'Used'.

clue.text: Working only briefly, the Jones boy getting confused

indicators.note: said briefly, words are cut short and lose their final letters
confused letters are jumbled out of their proper order

blocks.note: only cut short
taken as written
initial of the surname
boy cut short

explanation.surface: The Jones lad works only for a short while before getting muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose parse: the abbreviations are trimmed and the last pieces mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the job is at work, actively engaged in their duties.

clue.text: May spots go round pitch?

indicators.note: going round turns things about, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister of the UK
acne is an outbreak of spots

explanation.surface: Is a teenager's acne going to spread around the football pitch?
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a verb or month but is Theresa May, British PM from 2016 to 2019. 'Pitch' is the verb, as in pitching a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch tents is to set up camp, so the verb meaning to settle into a camp fits.

clue.text: With British deserting, abandon a vessel

indicators.note: one who deserts leaves, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
to abort a mission is to abandon it
taken as written

explanation.surface: With the British crew gone, the order is given to abandon ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but here it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, a blood vessel carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Depart quickly from USA flight in bad weather, leaving Florida

indicators.note: leaving here means departing from the word, so those letters are dropped
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: hail is bad weather
taken as written
FL is the postal code for Florida

explanation.surface: A traveller hurries to leave Florida on a US flight before a storm hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From USA' is part of the definition: the word is American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The American slang verb, usually followed by 'it', means to leave in a great hurry, like a fleeing animal.

clue.text: Cake or drink served in most of France at one time

indicators.note: most of something is all but a bit of it, so the final letter goes
something served in a vessel is placed inside it

blocks.note: Gaul was the Roman name for the region that became France
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Cake or a drink offered across most of historic France.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the answer is a French word for cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gâteau is a rich layered cream cake, a type of cake named from the French.

clue.text: Stroke cut wildly is making the boundary

indicators.note: something done wildly is uncontrolled, so the letters scatter into a new order
letters that form a boundary sit around the outside, enclosing the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket shot slashed wildly reaches the boundary for four.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture, a cut shot to the boundary, hides a medical meaning of 'Stroke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictus is the medical term for a sudden attack such as a stroke or seizure, and also a metrical beat.

clue.text: Consume ducks, as they naturally do

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the feathers ducks have on, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: to use up or erode gradually
second meaning: ducks are dressed in soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: Eating up as much as a duck does.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks are covered in down, soft under-feathers, so read literally they have it on.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode gradually is to consume, and ducks literally have soft feathers on as their natural clothing.

clue.text: Agreement in the form of free entertainment?

blocks.note: surface reading: a formal pact between nations

blocks.clueFragment: in the form of free entertainment?
blocks.note: setter's reading: an adjective formed by adding -y to a word for a free outing paid by someone else

explanation.surface: A deal that comes packaged as a free night out.
explanation.walkthrough: A treat is free entertainment, and adding Y makes a jokey adjective meaning 'treat-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between states is a pact signed by both parties, the usual sense of the word.

clue.text: Expose caterer, regularly hiding vermin

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
something hiding another keeps it tucked inside

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: A journalist exposes a caterer who keeps concealing a rodent problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expose' looks like revealing wrongdoing, but here it means expose to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is to expose something to air, such as soil or liquid, letting air pass through.

clue.text: Follows a band from the 60s

blocks.note: first meaning: tails someone secretly
second meaning: the British instrumental group that backed Cliff Richard

explanation.surface: Someone is a fan of a 1960s pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shadows were Cliff Richard's British backing group, famous for 'Apache'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone closely and covertly is to tail them, and the British guitar group bore this name.
